dataset.name: UAB resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma cohort (GSE79668)
dataset.description: Independent pancreatic adenocarcinoma cohort with bulk RNA sequencing of resected tumors and individual overall-survival follow-up.
dataset.cohort_context: The release contains 51 clinically annotated pancreatic adenocarcinomas collected from patients undergoing surgical resection. It is the tissue subseries of GSE79670; the fourteen pancreatic cell lines in GSE79669 are excluded. The patient cohort is independent of TCGA-PAAD and of the ICGC PACA-AU/PACA-CA validation options.

metadata.source_program: University of Alabama at Birmingham resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma cohort
metadata.library_method: Paired-end bulk RNA-seq from resected pancreatic adenocarcinoma tissue
metadata.redistribution_note: The GEO count matrix is analyzable in TRACE Explorer, but direct matrix redistribution remains disabled because GEO access alone does not resolve all submitter intellectual-property claims.
metadata.curation_note: All 51 tumor records have positive survival time and explicit vital status; 45 are deaths and six are censored. Matrix labels omit sequencing-run suffixes present in GEO titles, so a pinned regular-expression rule removes only an optional _T plus the terminal _SL run identifier. Library sizes are calculated across all 48,956 released count rows before log2(CPM + 1). The pinned GENCODE v9 annotation maps every Ensembl row; 334 symbols represented by more than one Ensembl row are excluded rather than combined, leaving 44,188 unambiguous genes.

expression.label: GEO counts normalized to log2(CPM + 1)
expression.mapping_source: Pinned GENCODE release 9 hg19 annotation declared by the source study
expression.duplicate_feature_rationale: Symbols mapped from more than one source Ensembl row are excluded rather than combined without an unambiguous gene-level rule.
expression.scale_note: TRACE Explorer computes each retained sample library size across all 48,956 pinned source rows, converts counts to CPM and applies log2(CPM + 1). Values are cohort-normalized and should not be compared directly with expression units from other releases.
